metadata.note: The Portsmouth, Great Falls and Conway Railroad (PGF&C) opened up the eastern White Mountains and Lake Winnipesaukee/Ossipee Lake region from the seacoast side, running Rollinsford/Somersworth (formerly called Great Falls) through Rochester, Union, Sanbornville, and Ossipee to North Conway and Intervale, where it connected with the Portland and Ogdensburg Railroad (see maine_central_mountain_division.geojson). Built in stages from 1849 (Great Falls-Rochester) through 1875 (Intervale); absorbed into the Eastern Railroad in 1878, then the Boston and Maine in 1890. Passenger service to Boston ended December 2, 1961. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap (active rail combined with abandoned/disused tagging); two stretches (Somersworth-Rochester and Rochester-Union, together about 31km) did not resolve to plausible connected paths in OSM's tagging for this corridor and are straight-line approximations between the real, correctly-ordered station towns -- flagged honestly rather than guessed at closer precision.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth,_Great_Falls_and_Conway_Railroad (operated Rollinsford-Intervale 1871-1890 as an independent entity, 67.1 miles; construction from Portsmouth to Union by 1854; Great Falls-Rochester opened Feb 28 1849; extended to South Milton 1850, Union 1855, West Ossipee 1871, North Conway 1872, Intervale by 1875; absorbed into Eastern Railroad 1878, then Boston and Maine 1890; passenger service to Boston ended December 2 1961)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging, Rollinsford to Intervale; routed via Dijkstra shortest path between each station's geocoded coordinates. The Somersworth-Rochester and Rochester-Union stretches did not resolve to plausible connected paths (implausible-detour check triggered) and are straight-line fallbacks.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact frequency/timetable for any era; precise opening dates for intermediate stations between the sourced segment-opening milestones.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
